## Along the gradient

The transect above is the spine of my research. Land use sets which small
mammals live where, which species meet people, and so where a virus crosses
over. Each programme below sits somewhere on it.

```{=html}
<ul class="card-grid">
  <li class="theme-card">
    <h3><a href="lassa/sierra_leone.html">Host ecology in Sierra Leone</a></h3>
    <p>Four years of small-mammal trapping across the gradient from forest to
    dwelling, and what land use does to the reservoir community.</p>
  </li>
  <li class="theme-card">
    <h3><a href="lassa/SCAPES.html">SCAPES, Nigeria</a></h3>
    <p>Human exposure to Lassa virus at village scale, and the behaviours that
    generate contact with rodents.</p>
  </li>
  <li class="theme-card">
    <h3><a href="lassa/lassa_urbanisation.html">Lassa fever and cities</a></h3>
    <p>What happens to spillover when the gradient runs into an expanding
    West African city.</p>
  </li>
  <li class="theme-card">
    <h3><a href="arha.html">Project ArHa</a></h3>
    <p>A global synthesis of arenavirus and hantavirus sampling in small
    mammals, and what surveillance bias hides.</p>
  </li>
  <li class="theme-card">
    <h3><a href="rodent_ecology/sintring.html">Bank voles at Uppsala</a></h3>
    <p>From September 2026, microbial sensors for the contact networks that
    drive environmental transmission.</p>
  </li>
  <li class="theme-card">
    <h3><a href="lassa/lassa_epidemiology.html">Lassa epidemiology</a></h3>
    <p>How many cases there really are, and what the sampling record can and
    cannot support.</p>
  </li>
</ul>
```

## Off the gradient

Work that does not sit on the transect: turning ecology into policy, building
tools other people can use, and outbreak response.

```{=html}
<ul class="card-grid">
  <li class="theme-card">
    <h3><a href="policy/vaccines.html">Vaccines and trial design</a></h3>
    <p>Designing trials for pathogens that arrive from wildlife, and the
    commitments that should govern self-disseminating vaccines.</p>
  </li>
  <li class="theme-card">
    <h3><a href="policy/surveillance.html">Surveillance and outbreak response</a></h3>
    <p>Where to sample when resources are finite. Plus earlier work on
    COVID-19 and mpox.</p>
  </li>
  <li class="theme-card">
    <h3><a href="open_science/tools.html">Open tools and data</a></h3>
    <p>Map Liberator, SiteTool, and a minimum data standard for wildlife
    disease research.</p>
  </li>
  <li class="theme-card">
    <h3><a href="rodent_ecology/lancet_pillars_view.html">Rodent-borne disease ecology</a></h3>
    <p>Three pillars for prevention: disease ecology, synanthropy and
    rodentation.</p>
  </li>
  <li class="theme-card">
    <h3><a href="consultancy.html">Consultancy</a></h3>
    <p>Quantitative epidemiology and disease modelling for health
    organisations and industry.</p>
  </li>
  <li class="theme-card">
    <h3><a href="others.html">Earlier work</a></h3>
    <p>Antimicrobial resistance, African swine fever, peste des petits
    ruminants and digital health.</p>
  </li>
</ul>
```
